identity.real_world_identity_notes: Pickup-bodied racer of the Brazilian Copa Chevrolet Montana, which ran from 2010 to 2012 as an access division to Stock Car Brasil. The cars used a tubular chassis built by JL Racing and a carburetted Chevrolet 5.7-litre V8 of 350 cv, shifted sequentially.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither.

The earlier record cited a community site for this car's transmission and power. That site is generated from Coanda's AMS2 spreadsheet and so describes the simulator, not the real car; Portuguese Wikipedia replaces it, and the power figure follows the source at 350 cv.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.copa-montana.20260814t192441105z-397e56ce by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered reference establishes the series and its sequential gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Portuguese Wikipedia gives the series car a sequential gearbox on a tubular JL Racing chassis, and the live drive selected five gears through a sequential stick with automatic cut and blip. The source does not state the gear count, so the five gears are the drive's result.

driver_summary: Sequential stick, one gear at a time. The car cuts the upshift and blips the downshift itself, so once you are rolling the gearbox asks nothing of your feet.
